question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & a & ∗ \\ -2 & b & ∗ \\ 1 & c & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $2a-b.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the Jordan matrix $J$ has a single $3\times 3$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =1,$ the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }{v}_{2}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-I\,}{\to }0\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =1,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}$ such that $(A-I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}.$

Now, computing $A-I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A-I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ -4 & 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{2}=3-2{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2-{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2-{x}_{3} \\ 3-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=0,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $2a-b=2\cdot 2-3=1.$
